target: Eu estou fazendo um curso online.
english: I'm taking an online course.
tip: To take a class or course, Portuguese uses fazer (to do), not 'tomar': fazendo um curso = taking a course.

target: Por que a loja está fechada?
english: Why is the store closed?
tip: 'Por que' (two words, no accent) = why (in questions). 'Porque' (one word) = because (in answers).

target: Por que você não veio ontem?
english: Why didn't you come yesterday?
tip: In questions, 'por que' is two words; the joined 'porque' answers them: 'Por que você não veio?' = why didn't you come?

target: Onde tem uma farmácia por perto?
english: Where is there a pharmacy nearby?
tip: In speech Brazilians use tem for 'there is': tem uma farmácia means 'there's a pharmacy'. The textbook há sounds formal.

target: Ele é muito gentil com todo mundo.
english: He's very kind to everyone.
tip: Personality traits use 'ser' – they're part of who you are. 'É gentil' = he's a kind person (inherently).

target: Ela está linda nesse vestido.
english: She looks beautiful in that dress.
tip: 'Estar bonita/linda' = she looks beautiful right now. 'Ser bonita/linda' = she IS beautiful (always). Both are compliments but with different nuances.

target: Onde posso carregar o celular?
english: Where can I charge my phone?
tip: 'Onde' = where. 'Aonde' = where to (with motion verbs): 'aonde você vai?'

target: Eu tenho uma reunião às dez.
english: I have a meeting at ten.
tip: Clock times use 'às': 'às dez' = at ten. It is 'a' plus feminine 'as,' since hours are feminine (as horas).

target: Ela dá conta de tudo sozinha.
english: She handles everything on her own.
tip: 'Dar conta de' means to handle or manage something: 'ela dá conta de tudo.' Literally 'to give account of.'

target: Eu vou perguntar para o garçom.
english: I'm going to ask the waiter.
tip: 'Perguntar' is to ask a question. To ask for something is 'pedir.' Here: 'perguntar para o garçom,' ask the waiter.

target: O que você comeu no almoço?
english: What did you eat for lunch?
tip: Regular -er verbs in the past drop -er and add -eu for he/she/you: comer becomes comeu (ate).

target: Nós vamos ao cinema hoje à noite.
english: We're going to the movies tonight.
tip: ao is the preposition a fused with o: vamos ao cinema means 'we go to the cinema'.

target: Ela vai de Uber para o trabalho.
english: She takes an Uber to work.
tip: Transport uses 'ir de': 'vai de Uber' = goes by Uber. Use 'de' for car, bus, or train. The one exception is 'a pé,' on foot.

target: Estou com vergonha de falar em público.
english: I'm embarrassed to speak in public.
tip: After a feeling noun, use de before the verb: vergonha de falar (embarrassed to speak), medo de cair (afraid to fall).

target: A festa é na casa do Pedro.
english: The party is at Pedro's house.
tip: Event locations use 'ser': 'a festa é na casa' = the party takes place at the house. This is about where the event happens, not where something is located.

target: O prato é típico do Nordeste.
english: The dish is typical of the Northeast.
tip: de + o contracts to do: típico do Nordeste (typical of the Northeast). You cannot keep them apart as 'de o.'

target: Eu faço isso todo dia sem pensar.
english: I do this every day without thinking.
tip: 'Sem' plus an infinitive equals English 'without' plus -ing: 'sem pensar' = without thinking.

target: Eu tenho certeza de que vai dar certo.
english: I'm sure it's going to work out.
tip: dar certo is literally 'to give right' and means to work out: vai dar certo says 'it is going to work out'.

target: Como eu chego na rodoviária?
english: How do I get to the bus station?
tip: In Brazil chegar (to arrive) takes em: chego na rodoviária. Formal or European usage prefers chegar a.

target: Por que o preço subiu tanto?
english: Why did the price go up so much?
tip: Por que in two words asks a question; porque in one word means because: Por que o preço subiu?

target: Ela é advogada, mas está trabalhando como professora.
english: She's a lawyer, but she's working as a teacher.
tip: ser for identity, estar for the moment: é advogada says what she is, está trabalhando what she is doing right now.

target: Ele é solteiro.
english: He's single.
tip: Marital status uses ser, not estar, even though it can change: ele e solteiro, ela e casada.

target: Quem ligou para você?
english: Who called you?
tip: ligar takes para, not a direct object: you call to someone in Portuguese. ligou para você is 'called you'.

target: Estou pronto para sair.
english: I'm ready to leave.
tip: pronto para + an infinitive means ready to do something: pronto para sair (ready to leave).

target: O leite está estragado.
english: The milk is spoiled.
tip: Estar marks a changed condition, so spoiled milk is o leite esta estragado, not e estragado.

target: Quem te contou isso?
english: Who told you that?
tip: In Brazil você (you) pairs with te for the object: quem te contou (who told you), mixing você with the older te.

target: O que tem para comer?
english: What is there to eat?
tip: 'O que tem' is an extremely casual and common way to ask what's available. Literally 'what does it have.'

target: Como se chama esse prato?
english: What's this dish called?
tip: 'Como se chama' literally means 'how does it call itself.' Use it for things and people: 'como se chama esse prato?' or 'como você se chama?'

target: Ela está grávida de seis meses.
english: She's six months pregnant.
tip: Even though pregnancy is temporary, 'estar grávida' is the standard expression – never use 'ser grávida'.

target: Qual é a sua comida favorita?
english: What's your favorite food?
tip: Portuguese uses 'qual e' where English says what is, to single one out: Qual e a sua comida favorita.
